description: Step one foot out to the side and back while the arms go up and down. Keep the chest tall and the feet quiet, with no jump.
March in place and lift the knees toward belly-button height. Stand tall and do not lean backward.
Turn the wrists as if you are swinging a rope and stay light on your feet. March on Starter, and use tiny hops only when landings are quiet.
Hop or step through an imaginary or drawn pattern, landing softly on one foot or two. Stand tall between hops.
Make smooth circles with the arms, first forward and then back. Keep the shoulders down and the neck long.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and soft knees, reaching toward the opposite shin. Do not round the back or force a toe-touch.
Walk the hands out to a straight plank line, then walk the feet in and stand tall. Do not hold a downward-dog shape.
Sit on a sturdy chair and stand up without using the hands, then sit down slowly. Keep the chest tall and the knees tracking over the toes.
Sit the hips back as if lowering toward a chair, then stand tall. Keep the heels down and the knees following the toes.
Step onto a low, stable step with the whole foot, stand tall, and step down slowly. Push through the heel and hold a rail if needed.
Lean the back against a wall and bend the knees to a comfortable depth. Keep breathing and do not hold the breath.
Hold a wall or chair, take a short step back, and lower until the back knee hovers. Keep the torso tall and the front knee over mid-foot.
Squat, jump forward, and land softly on both feet with bent knees. Stick the landing and keep it quiet.
Crouch, then jump with the arms and legs wide like a star. Land quietly with soft knees.
With a flat back like a table, take small steps with opposite hand and foot. Starter may keep the knees down.
Lift the hips and walk on hands and feet with the chest facing up. Keep the hips high and do not hang the head back.
From hands and knees, reach one arm and the opposite leg long, not high. Keep the back flat and the hips level.
Lie on the belly and lift the arms and legs just a little, then lower. Keep the eyes on the floor and the neck long.
Lie on the belly and lift the arms into a Y, then a T, with the thumbs up. Keep the forehead down and squeeze the shoulder blades.
Stand with heels, bottom, shoulders, and head lightly touching a wall. Keep the chin level and breathe.
With the back and head on a wall, slide the arms up and down slowly. Move only as far as the back stays on the wall.
Stand on one leg with the other knee up and the hands on the hips. Look at one spot, and touch a wall if you need to.
March slowly in place with an easy arm swing. Breathe in and out and let the heart rate come down.
Step side to side and tap the other foot in, swinging the arms comfortably. Stay tall and keep the steps soft.
Rise onto the balls of both feet, then lower slowly. Stand tall and hold a wall if you need balance.
Walk forward on the balls of the feet, keeping the heels off the floor. Stand tall and take short, controlled steps.
Walk forward on the heels, keeping the toes up. Stand tall and go slowly.
Lie on the back with bent knees and lift the hips, then lower slowly. Squeeze the seat at the top and do not arch the low back.
Stand tall, hold a wall, and lift one leg out to the side, then lower slowly. Keep the torso still and the toes pointing forward.
Lie on the back with arms up and knees bent, then lower one arm and the opposite leg without losing a flat back. Move slowly and keep the ribs down.
Place the hands on a wall and bend the elbows to bring the chest toward the wall, then press back. Keep the body in a straight line.
Sit or stand tall and squeeze the shoulder blades together, then relax. Do not shrug the shoulders up toward the ears.
Raise the arms up and out into a Y shape, then lower slowly. Keep the thumbs slightly up and the ribs down.
Step side to side in a small skating pattern without jumping. Reach the back foot lightly and keep the chest tall.
Shuffle sideways with soft knees and quick, small steps. Do not bounce or cross the feet.
Jog or march in place and kick the heels toward the seat. Stay tall and land softly.
Tap the feet quickly in place as if the floor is hot. Stay light, keep the chest tall, and use a short burst.
Hold a wall and draw slow circles with the toes, then switch direction and switch feet. Keep the leg relaxed.
Stand facing a wall with the back heel down and lean forward gently. Stop at a mild stretch and do not bounce.
Stand facing a low step and tap one foot, then the other, on top of the step. Stay tall and keep the taps light.
Walk in a straight line, placing the heel of one foot just in front of the toes of the other. Look ahead and use a wall if you wobble.
Walk backward in a clear space, stepping carefully and standing tall. Look over the shoulder as needed and go slowly.
Swing the arms forward and back in a relaxed rhythm. Keep the shoulders down and the chest tall.
Put the hands on the hips or across the chest, push the hips back, then stand tall. Keep a soft knee bend and a flat back.
Hold a straight line from head to heels or knees for a short time. Do not let the hips sag or pike up.
From hands and knees, tap one shoulder with the opposite hand, then switch. Keep the hips still.
Jump the feet out and in while the arms go up and down. Land softly, and use Step Jacks instead if landings are loud.
Push the hips back as if closing a car door with your seat, then stand tall. Keep the back flat and the knees soft.
